meta.title: Words in an average daily newspaper

prompt: How many words are there in an average daily newspaper?

clarifications.answer: Assume a page of 12 in x 20 in (240 sq in) and 24 pages total, of which 4 are almost entirely images (negligible text).
About a third of a page is illustrations; after removing images, borders and column spacing, assume ~100 sq in of net text area per page.
Assume ~30 words per sq in for body text and ~8 for headings, with body/heading area split 90/10.
Only the ~20 text pages carry words; count words per page then scale to those pages.

common_traps: Multiplying full page area by word density without removing images, borders and column gaps.
Using one word density for both body text and headings.
Counting all 24 pages instead of only the ~20 pages that actually carry text.

anchors.1: Guesses a number with no area-to-words reasoning.
anchors.3: Uses area x density but on gross page area, not net text area.
anchors.5: Derives net text area per page, applies body/heading densities, then scales to text pages.

anchors.1: No separation of text from non-text space.
anchors.3: Removes images but ignores borders or column spacing.
anchors.5: Separates images, borders and spacing, and splits remaining area into body vs heading text.

anchors.1: Density-times-area math is off; lands orders of magnitude away.
anchors.3: Reaches a number with a slip, landing just outside 40000-70000.
anchors.5: Carries the per-page and page-count math cleanly, landing near 55000 words.

anchors.3: Mentions a check but does not complete it.
anchors.5: Back-checks via articles: ~55000 words at ~250 words each implies ~200 articles, which is reasonable.
